title: rotini contract document
description: The contract document `rotini generate` writes when the conf sets generate.contract: every command of a cli with its inputs, output and exit statuses. Each command maps directly onto a tool definition for an AI agent: `name` and `summary` describe it, `parameters` is the JSON Schema of its arguments and flags, and `output` the JSON Schema of its result. Hidden commands and inputs are listed with `hidden: true`; a tool that presents the cli's public surface skips them. Every embedded schema is standard JSON Schema (draft-07). `parameters`, `output`, an exit status's `output` and `stdin.schema` are self-contained: each declares `$schema` and carries the definitions it reaches. A per-input `schema` may `$ref` a definition, which resolves against this document's `definitions`. Newer rotini releases add fields to this format, so validate a contract with the schema-contract.json from the rotini that wrote it.

format.description: The document's format and its version. A change that would break a reader changes the number.

commands.description: Every command, the root first and then depth-first in spec order. A hidden command, and everything beneath it, is marked `hidden: true`. A plugin a command declares follows it, with `plugin: true`.

definitions.description: The spec's named schemas, as JSON Schema, by name, and those of the specs it composes. A composed spec's schema whose name is already taken by a different schema is listed as `<spec name>.<schema name>`, and that spec's references name it so.

errors.description: The JSON Schema of one line rotini.StructuredReporter writes to stderr: an error, warning, info or success. A program uses that reporter only when its author opts in.

completion.description: What the program's shell completion lets its users switch. Present only when the cli declares something here.

messages_env.description: The environment variable that hides completion messages when set to 0, false or off.

descriptions_env.description: The environment variable that hides the descriptions shown beside completion candidates when set to 0, false or off.

response_files.description: How the program reads response files: before the first `--`, a word starting with the prefix is replaced by the named file's lines, one argument per line. A caller passing an argument that starts with the prefix writes it after `--`, or doubles the prefix (`@@x` is the argument `@x`). Present only when the cli reads response files.

prefix.description: The character that starts a response-file word, such as @.

multicall.description: How the program dispatches on the name its binary was invoked as, through links or copies. With neither field, busybox style: a binary named after a top-level command runs it. Present only when the cli declares multicall; removing or changing it breaks installed links.

prefix.description: Stripped from the invoked name before it is matched against the top-level commands.

complete.description: An invoked name starting with this answers shell completion for the root, in the plugin hosts' format unless the program sets another.

topics.description: The help topics the root declares: pages that aren't commands, shown by `<name> help <topic>` when the program has a help command that calls the generated Help function. Present only when the cli declares any.

name.description: The command as typed, the root included: "taskr list".

path.description: The command names below the root: ["list"]. Empty for the root.

hidden.description: true when the command, or one of its ancestors, is hidden: it runs, but help leaves it out.

deprecated.description: Why the command is deprecated, when it is.

deprecated_since.description: The release that deprecated the command.

removed_in.description: The release that will remove the command.

deprecated_identifiers.description: The aliases that are deprecated. Running the command by one of them still works.

deprecated_identifiers_removed_in.description: The release that will remove each deprecated alias, by alias.

plugin.description: true for a plugin: a separate program the command runs, whose inputs and output this document does not describe.

options_first.description: true when flags must come before the command's first argument: every word after that argument is an argument, flag-shaped words and `--` included.

passthrough.description: true when every word after the command's name is an argument, taken as typed: the command parses no flags of its own.

flags.description: The command's own flags, then the cascading flags it inherits from its ancestors.

flag_groups.description: Rules over sets of the command's flags, by flag name.

flag_dependencies.description: Flags that require others, by flag name.

config_files.description: The configuration files this command declares. The command and every command beneath it read them; a config entry's `file` names one by `name`.

parameters.description: An object schema with one property per visible argument and flag, by name, each carrying its description (else its summary) as `description`: the input schema of a tool definition. Hidden inputs are left out. Self-contained.

output.description: The shape of what the command writes to stdout when it succeeds, when it declares one. A command that writes a stream of items declares one item. Self-contained.

stream.description: true when the command writes a stream of `output` items rather than one value: in JSON, one compact value per line; in YAML, one document per item, each starting `---`.

hidden_aliases.description: More names that run the command but that help, completion and suggestions never list.

replaced_by.description: With `deprecated`: the command to use instead, as its command names below the root joined by spaces ("purge", "remote add").

stability.description: How settled the command is, as declared. Its inputs, sub-commands, output and exit codes are at most as stable as it is.

effects.description: What running the command does, as declared. Absent says nothing: assume the worst (destructive, reaching outside the machine). Sub-commands don't inherit it; a flag's `effects` can raise it for a run that gives the flag.

variadic.description: true when it takes every remaining positional. When arguments follow it, they take the last positionals and it takes the ones in between.

passthrough.description: true when raw words start at this argument: it and every word after it are taken as typed, flag-shaped words and `--` included. A word starting with - that should be its first word is written after `--`.

env.description: The environment variables the argument falls back to when the command line leaves its position empty, in lookup order: the first one set wins.

config_key.description: The config file key the argument falls back to after its environment variables. Present only when the command reads config files.

schema.description: The value's JSON Schema. A `$ref` in it resolves against the document's `definitions`.

glob.description: true when, on Windows, each word containing `*`, `?` or `[` is expanded into the paths it matches (the shell does it elsewhere). A word that names an existing path, or matches nothing, is kept as written.

values_from.description: The place in the command's output whose field names are this input's allowed values (`output`, `output.tasks`): the enum in its `schema` (on `items` for a list) lists them, sorted, and changes when the output's fields do.

description.description: Longer text about the input, paragraphs separated by blank lines. It is the input's description in `parameters` when set, else its summary is.

negated.description: The forms that set a negatable bool flag false: ["--no-color"]. They take no value.

cascading.description: true when the command declares it and every command beneath it accepts it too.

inherited.description: true when an ancestor declares it as cascading.

short_circuit.description: true when setting it on the command line waives the command's required inputs and other rules, as --help does: an agent can pass it without supplying anything else.

env.description: The environment variables the flag falls back to when it is not on the command line, in lookup order: the first one set wins.

config_key.description: The config file key the flag falls back to after its environment variables. Present only when the command reads config files.

from.description: Where a value typed on the command line may come from besides the text itself: `file`, a value starting with @ is replaced by that file's contents (@@ is a literal @); `stdin`, a value of exactly - is replaced by what is piped on stdin. A secret flag whose list leaves out `value` refuses any other value typed on the command line: pass the secret through a file or stdin.

implicit_value.description: The value the flag takes when given without one: its value is optional and, when given, must be attached (`--color=never`, not `--color never`).

dotted_keys.description: true when a map flag's dotted key (`--set a.b=1`) assigns into nested maps.

deprecated_identifiers.description: The identifiers that are deprecated, when only some are. Without it, a deprecated flag is deprecated under every identifier.

deprecated_identifiers_removed_in.description: The release that will remove each deprecated identifier, by identifier.

schema.description: The value's JSON Schema. A `$ref` in it resolves against the document's `definitions`.

repeatable.description: false when giving the flag more than once on the command line is an error rather than the last value winning. Absent means repeats are accepted.

role.description: What the flag means to a program driving the CLI. force: the bool flag that lets the command replace existing output files. fields: the list flag that chooses which output fields are written. sort: the flag that names the output field to sort by. These three change nothing at run time. chdir: the root flag naming the directory the run resolves relative paths and config discovery against, read from the command line only; a caller passes an absolute path, or one relative to its own directory. dry-run: the bool flag that previews a run without changing anything. confirm: the bool flag that answers yes for a command that would otherwise refuse or prompt. machine-output: the flag that makes the command write its output as JSON, a bool flag or a string flag whose `role_value` selects JSON. page: the flag that selects a page of results.

role_value.description: With role machine-output on a string flag: the value that selects JSON (`--format=json`).

effects.description: What giving the flag adds to its command's effects, as declared: a run's kind is the highest of its command's and every given flag's; it is idempotent only when every stated value is, and reaches outside the machine when any does. A cascading flag raises whichever command it is given to.

hidden_identifiers.description: More identifiers the command line accepts for the flag, which help, completion and suggestions never list. A negatable flag's hidden long identifiers have unlisted --no- forms too.

replaced_by.description: With `deprecated`: the identifier of the flag to use instead ("--output").

flag_set.description: The flag set the flag comes from, when the spec declares it once in a set that several commands use. The flag works like the command's own.

values_from.description: The place in the command's output whose field names are this flag's allowed values (`output`, `output.tasks`): the enum in its `schema` (on `items` for a list) lists them, sorted, and changes when the output's fields do.

description.description: Longer text about the input, paragraphs separated by blank lines. It is the input's description in `parameters` when set, else its summary is.

variables.description: The environment variables read, the first preferred.

kind.description: How the value is written: a list is split on its `separator`, else commas (TAGS=a,b); a map is key=value pairs split the same way.

secret.description: true when the value is a secret; its default is then left out.

nesting.description: The separator that gathers a family of variables into one nested map: with variable ACME_HTTP and nesting __, ACME_HTTP__RETRY__MAX=9 sets {retry: {max: "9"}}.

schema.description: The value's JSON Schema. A `$ref` in it resolves against the document's `definitions`.

separator.description: The character a list or map variable is split on, when not a comma: a plain split with spaces trimmed (`:` reads PATHS=a:b).

description.description: Longer text about the input, paragraphs separated by blank lines. It is the input's description in `parameters` when set, else its summary is.

key.description: The key read from the configuration file.

file.description: The name of the configuration file it is read from, when one is named.

schema.description: The value's JSON Schema. A `$ref` in it resolves against the document's `definitions`.

description.description: Longer text about the input, paragraphs separated by blank lines. It is the input's description in `parameters` when set, else its summary is.

format.description: How stdin is read: json, yaml, toml, text, lines, jsonl (one JSON record per line; `schema` describes one record) or bytes (exactly as piped).

required.description: true when an empty stdin is an error.

schema.description: The shape of what is read. Self-contained.

stream.description: true when lines or jsonl records are read one at a time as the command consumes them, so stdin of any size is read in constant memory.

separator.description: nul: lines are separated by NUL bytes, as `find -print0` writes them, instead of line endings.

unless_argument.description: The argument, by name, that stands in for stdin: stdin is read only when it gets no value, or `-`. Absent means stdin is read on every run.

name.description: The code's snake_case name, unique within the command.

retryable.description: true when running the same command again may succeed.

output.description: What the command still writes to stdout when it exits with this code. Self-contained.

docs_url.description: A link to more about the code.

EnumValues.description: What each of the input's enum values declares beyond its spelling, by value. Present only when some value declares more than its spelling. The schema's own `enum` lists the values only, hidden ones left out.

summary.description: One line saying what the value means.

aliases.description: Other spellings accepted for the value, each bound as the value.

deprecated_aliases.description: The aliases being retired; still accepted.

hidden.description: true when the value is accepted but not offered or listed.

deprecated.description: The value's deprecation message; the value is still accepted.

deprecated_since.description: The release that deprecated the value.

removed_in.description: The release that will remove the value.

RotiniType.description: The input's type as rotini reads it: a Go type (`int8`, `[]string`, `map[string]int`) or a rotini value type (`duration`, `date`, `count`), the JSON Schema names written as Go types (`integer` is `int`). Absent for a named object schema, which `schema` references. JSON Schema's `integer` cannot tell `int8` from `int64`; this can. `inputfile` and `outputfile` are paths where `-` means stdin and stdout.

Kind.description: How a caller supplies the value. scalar: one value. count: repeat the identifier (`-vvv`), never `=N`. list: repeat the input, or split one value on its separator. map: key=value pairs. object: a named object schema, given as JSON or field by field (`--db.host x`).

Separator.description: The character each value is split on: `--tags a,b` is two tags. The word nul means NUL bytes, which only a flag's file or stdin content can hold.

IgnoreCase.description: true when an enum value matches whatever its case.

Layouts.description: How a time value is written: Go reference-time layouts (2006-01-02, 2006-01-02T15:04:05Z07:00), or unix (seconds since the epoch) or unixmilli. Present on time inputs only.

Secret.description: true when the value is a secret; its default is then left out.

Hidden.description: true when help leaves the input out. It is still read. Absent from the command's `parameters`.

ConfigSource.description: The configuration file whose path this input supplies, by its `config_files` name.

kind.description: The rule: mutually_exclusive, at most one set; required_together, all or none; one_of, exactly one; at_least_one, one or more.

flags.description: The flags it covers, by name.

FlagDependency.description: A rule that applies when `when` is set on the command line (with one of the `equals` values, when given) and none of `unless` is: then every flag in `requires` must be set and none in `forbids` may be. Only what the command line sets counts; defaults and fallbacks neither trigger a rule nor satisfy it.

when.description: The flag that, when set, triggers the rule, by name. Absent when only `unless` decides.

requires.description: The flags it requires, by name.

equals.description: The values of `when` that trigger the rule; absent means any value.

unless.description: Flags, by name, any one of which set on the command line turns the rule off.

forbids.description: The flags that can't be set when the rule applies, by name.

format.description: The file's format, when declared; otherwise its extension says.

path.description: A fixed path, which may start with ~.

discover.description: How the file is found at run time, instead of a fixed path.

strategy.description: walk-up: from the working directory upward. xdg: $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/<app>, else ~/.config/<app>. native: the platform's config directory (~/Library/Application Support/<app> on macOS, %AppData%\<app> on Windows, as xdg elsewhere). xdg-system: each directory of $XDG_CONFIG_DIRS (default /etc/xdg) joined with <app>.

as.description: env: a dotenv file whose entries are environment variables, under the real environment (which wins); it supplies no config keys.

profiles.description: The file holds named profiles, one chosen per run. The chosen profile's keys win over the file's other top-level keys, which every profile shares.

under.description: The top-level key holding the profiles.

select.description: What chooses the profile: the flag set on the command line, then the first set variable.

default.description: The profile used when nothing chooses one; without it, only the shared keys apply.

PluginDiscovery.description: The command runs any executable named <prefix><word> as `<command> <word>`.

hidden.description: true when completion leaves discovered plugins out.

Relative.description: The time input also takes a time measured from now. past: `2h` or `3d` ago, `now`, `today`, `yesterday`. future: `2h` or `+2h` from now, `tomorrow`. both: a sign is required (`-2h`, `+3d`). Present on time inputs only.

VariableFile.description: An environment variable naming a file that holds the value (`APP_TOKEN_FILE=/run/secrets/token`), for when the variable itself isn't set. Setting both is an error.

Expand.description: What is expanded in the input's values, from every source, before they are checked: home, a leading `~` or `~name`; env, `$NAME` and `${NAME}` (an unset variable is an error). Absent: values are taken as written.

RelativeTo.description: config: a relative path read from a configuration file is resolved against that file's directory. Values from other sources stay relative to the run's directory.

Stability.description: How settled the item is, as declared. experimental: it may change or be removed in any release. beta: it may change in a minor release. Absent means stable. An item is at most as stable as its command and that command's ancestors.

name.description: The word after `help` that shows the topic.

body.description: The topic's text, when it is written in the spec.

generate.description: What the topic's text is built from, when it is generated. environment: every environment variable the program reads.

kind.description: read: changes nothing. write: creates or changes things. destructive: deletes or overwrites what can't be got back.

idempotent.description: Whether running it again with the same inputs changes nothing more. Absent says nothing.

open_world.description: Whether it reaches the network or other systems outside the machine. Absent says nothing: assume it does.

Agent.description: As declared: true offers the item to AI agents (tool exports, the agent skill page, permission snippets) where it would be left out by default; false keeps it, and a command's sub-commands, from them. Absent follows the defaults.
